definition: a departure from what is normal or expected, usually a brief one
examples: The spike in prices proved to be an aberration.
He dismissed the result as a statistical aberration.

definition: although, used to add a qualifying remark in a compact way
examples: He agreed, albeit reluctantly.
The method works, albeit slowly.

definition: something that does not fit the usual pattern and therefore invites explanation
examples: The reading was an anomaly, not a trend.
Astronomers noticed an anomaly in the orbit.

definition: plain and without comfort or decoration, or severe in manner
examples: The room was clean but austere.
She kept an austere daily routine.

definition: to find a way around a rule or an obstacle instead of confronting it
examples: The design circumvents the patent.
They circumvented the ban by moving offshore.

definition: clear and convincing because the reasoning holds together
examples: She made a cogent case for delay.
The objection is cogent and deserves an answer.

definition: helping to make a particular result more likely
examples: The noise was not conducive to study.
Warm evenings are conducive to long conversation.

definition: to support a statement with independent evidence
examples: Two witnesses corroborated her account.
Nothing in the file corroborates the claim.

definition: to describe or mark out something precisely
examples: The report delineates three possible routes.
Responsibilities are clearly delineated.

definition: so different in kind that comparison is difficult
examples: The book draws on disparate sources.
Disparate groups united behind one demand.

definition: drawing on a wide and varied range of sources or styles
examples: Her reading is eclectic.
The menu is eclectic but coherent.

definition: based on observation or experiment rather than on theory alone
examples: The claim lacks empirical support.
Empirical work followed the model by a decade.

definition: lasting only a very short time
examples: Fame of that kind is ephemeral.
The blossom is beautiful and ephemeral.

definition: deliberately unclear, so that more than one reading stays open
examples: The minister gave an equivocal reply.
Results were equivocal and required repetition.

definition: to make an already bad situation worse
examples: The delay exacerbated the shortage.
Shouting only exacerbates the problem.

definition: stated openly and in detail, leaving nothing implied
examples: The contract is explicit about deadlines.
She gave explicit instructions.

definition: to estimate something unknown by extending a known pattern
examples: You cannot extrapolate from a single case.
They extrapolated the trend to 2040.

definition: existing as a permanent and inseparable part of something
examples: There is an inherent risk in the method.
Ambiguity is inherent in natural language.

definition: harmless, and unlikely to cause offence or damage
examples: It was an innocuous remark.
The substance is innocuous in small amounts.

definition: to place two things side by side so that the contrast becomes visible
examples: The exhibition juxtaposes old and new photographs.
He juxtaposes the two claims without comment.

definition: showing great care about small details
examples: She kept meticulous notes.
The restoration was meticulous.

definition: existing in name only, or very small compared with the real value
examples: He is the nominal head of the firm.
There is a nominal fee for entry.

definition: to make something harder to understand, often on purpose
examples: The wording obfuscates the real cost.
Jargon can obfuscate rather than explain.

definition: a framework of assumptions that shapes how a field understands its subject
examples: The discovery shifted the prevailing paradigm.
Both papers work within the same paradigm.

definition: spread through every part of something
examples: The smell of smoke was pervasive.
Distrust had become pervasive.

definition: dealing with things in a practical way rather than by theory or principle
examples: They took a pragmatic view of the deadline.
The decision was pragmatic, not ideological.

definition: not securely held, and likely to fall or fail
examples: The ladder was in a precarious position.
Their finances remain precarious.

definition: to make something impossible in advance
examples: The clause precludes any refund.
Illness precluded her from travelling.

definition: to increase rapidly in number and spread widely
examples: Copies of the file proliferated online.
Small workshops proliferated in the district.

definition: careful to avoid unnecessary risk, especially with time or money
examples: It would be prudent to wait.
She made prudent choices early on.

definition: not needed because it repeats something already present
examples: The final paragraph is redundant.
Two of the checks are redundant.

definition: able to recover quickly after difficulty or damage
examples: The local economy proved resilient.
Children are more resilient than we assume.

definition: most noticeable or most important among many details
examples: Let me repeat the salient points.
The salient fact is the timing.

definition: seeming genuine or valid but in fact false
examples: The correlation turned out to be spurious.
He made a spurious claim of ownership.

definition: understood or agreed without being said openly
examples: There was tacit approval from the board.
They reached a tacit understanding.

definition: very weak or thin, and therefore easily broken or doubted
examples: The link between the two is tenuous.
She kept a tenuous hold on the lead.

definition: found everywhere, so common that it stops being noticed
examples: Screens are now ubiquitous.
The phrase became ubiquitous within a year.

definition: never having happened before, so there is no earlier case to compare with
examples: The rainfall was unprecedented.
She won by an unprecedented margin.

definition: to show that someone was right or free from blame after doubt
examples: The later results vindicated her caution.
He was vindicated by the inquiry.

definition: to be a good enough reason for something
examples: The evidence warrants a second look.
Nothing in the file warrants dismissal.
